name: John Laird
title: California State Senator
district: California State Senate District 17 (Santa Cruz, San Benito, and Monterey Counties, and the majority of San Luis Obispo County)
years_of_service: 2020 to present (California State Senate); first elected November 2020, took office December 7, 2020, re-elected November 2024 for a final term under Senate term limits
background: Laird's career in California politics spans more than four decades. He was first elected to the Santa Cruz City Council in 1981 as the top vote-getter in an eight-candidate field, was re-elected in 1985, and served until being termed out in 1990; the council selected him for one-year mayoral terms in 1983-1984 and 1987-1988, making him one of the first openly gay mayors in the United States. During this period he also worked as executive director of the Santa Cruz AIDS Project.

From 1994 to 2002 he served on the Cabrillo College Board of Trustees. He was then elected to the California State Assembly representing District 27 (parts of Santa Clara, Santa Cruz, and Monterey Counties), winning the general election in 2002 with 61.4% of the vote and winning re-election in 2004 (68.7%) and 2006 (70.2%) before being termed out in 2008 after three terms. His official Senate biography states he authored 82 bills signed into law during his Assembly service.

Governor Jerry Brown appointed Laird Secretary of the California Natural Resources Agency, a cabinet post he held from January 5, 2011 to January 7, 2019, overseeing roughly 25 departments, boards, and conservancies and a budget in the billions of dollars covering parks, wildlife, water, and coastal policy.

Laird was elected to California State Senate District 17 in November 2020, defeating Republican Vicki Nohrden 64.7% to 35.3%, and was re-elected in November 2024 with 65.0% of the vote against Republican Tony Virrueta; Senate term limits make this his final term. He chairs the Senate Budget and Fiscal Review Committee and, in that capacity, was Lead Senate author of ACA 20, the constitutional amendment that placed Proposition 2 on the 2026 statewide ballot.

voting_record_highlights: ACA 20 (2025-2026 session): as Lead Senate author, voted Aye when the Senate passed ACA 20 by a 29-2 floor vote on June 25, 2026, placing the measure on the November 2026 ballot as Proposition 2.

SB 272 (2023): authored and voted for this bill requiring coastal and San Francisco Bay-area local governments to adopt sea level rise adaptation plans by January 1, 2034; signed into law and chaptered October 7, 2023.

SB 283 (2025), the Clean Energy Safety Act of 2025: authored and voted for this bill setting fire-safety inspection and siting requirements for battery energy storage systems; signed into law and chaptered October 6, 2025.

As Senate Budget and Fiscal Review Committee chair, authored and voted for the annual Budget Act appropriations bills for the 2025-2026 session (e.g., SB 106, amending the Budget Act of 2025 for healthcare workforce and family planning appropriations; signed into law February 11, 2026).
